_comment: Mirror of EA Netherlands' human-translated glossary at
This is the single largest quality risk removed from the Dutch-generation
problem, because it is exactly the artefact that needed a native speaker
and now does not need generating. It is authoritative: do NOT generate a
glossary, and do not let a model invent an alternative rendering for any
The `keepInEnglish` list is the part that would otherwise have required a
Dutch speaker. There is no rule an LLM could infer — it is a set of
house-style judgements someone already made. Left to itself a model will
produce something like 'verdienen om te geven', which is wrong and reads
as a machine translation on sight.
Refresh with `npm run mirror-glossary`, which re-reads the published page.
Verified against the page contents as described in the spec, 5 Aug 2026.

framework.name: ITN-raamwerk
framework.note: The spine for /vacatures/waarom-deze-banen (§9.5). Established EA NL house vocabulary rather than something the board invents.

dimensions.question: Hoe groot is het probleem — hoeveel leed of verlies gaat ermee gepaard?
Kun je er iets aan doen? Levert extra inzet meetbaar resultaat op?
Hoeveel mensen en geld gaan er al naartoe? Waar is de eerstvolgende euro het meest waard?

fourth.question: Hoeveel verandert er door déze functie, meer dan door het werk van één persoon?
fourth.note: The fourth thing this board looks at that ITN alone does not capture (§9.5).

organisations.note: Nederlandse gemeenschap van mensen die een vast deel van hun inkomen weggeven. Heette tot 2026 de Tien Procent Club — gebruik de oude naam niet meer.
